chunk_findings.detail: The reserved-only filter triggers when either ordinary share is exhausted, but the flight and worktree caps are independent: an ordinary candidate that does not use a worktree consumes only the flight cap. Example: `parallel.limit=2`, `cfg.worktree.max_parallel=1`, and one live ordinary item with a worktree gives `free.ordinary_flight=1` but `free.ordinary_tree=0`; the `any(...)` sees `0`, returns only reserved ids, and drops an ordinary non-worktree ready item even though there is an ordinary flight slot for it. The filter must account for whether the candidate consumes the exhausted cap, not reduce selection to reserved work based on either cap alone.

For example, with `cfg.worktree.enabled=True`, `cfg.worktree.max_parallel=1`, one existing live worktree, and a task limit of 3, `flight_slots=2` and `tree_slots=0`; since `slots != flight_slots`, `_plan` enters that `else` and raises `NameError: name 'tree_cap' is not defined` instead of returning the blocked plan.

chunk_findings.detail: With worktree disabled, `open_slots` returns `free.ordinary_tree = None` (the exact case the previous `shares` guard in `_candidates` existed to avoid). If `free.ordinary_flight` is not `None`, `_fits` computes `tree = free.ordinary_tree` and then evaluates `tree > 0` in `return flight > 0 and (tree > 0 or not needs_tree(it))`. chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite drops the `share is not None` guard that `_candidates` used on `free.ordinary_tree`. `_fits` now does `tree > 0` whenever `needs_tree(it)` is true. `ordinary_tree` / `tree` are still absent (None) when the worktree cap is off — that is why the old code skipped a None share. With worktrees disabled, a free flight slot, and a ready item that is not tagged `no-worktree`, `flight > 0` is true and `None > 0` raises TypeError, so `ddflow next --lane` crashes instead of offering the item. chunk_findings.detail: The refactor into `caps()` deletes the local `paused = parallel is not None and parallel.admit_paused` assignment, but the rest of `plan` still reads `paused` in the no-slot/pause branch after the cap computation. Concretely, `plan(state, cfg, live, None)` with `in_flight >= cfg.schedule.max_parallel_tasks` produces `slots == 0` and then evaluates `paused`, which is now unbound, raising `NameError` instead of reporting the schedule cap. Unpack `paused = c.paused` alongside the other `Caps` fields.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py:plan

chunk_findings.detail: With worktree disabled, `open_slots` returns `free.ordinary_tree = None` (the exact case the previous `shares` guard in `_candidates` existed to avoid). If `free.ordinary_flight` is not `None`, `_fits` computes `tree = free.ordinary_tree` and then evaluates `tree > 0` in `return flight > 0 and (tree > 0 or not needs_tree(it))`. Since Python evaluates `tree > 0` first, this raises `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'`. Any `ddflow next --lane` call with `[worktree]` disabled and a ready ordinary candidate hits this instead of returning an offer; the previous code guarded `share is not None` for precisely this disabled-tree case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/pull.py:_fits

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite drops the `share is not None` guard that `_candidates` used on `free.ordinary_tree`. `_fits` now does `tree > 0` whenever `needs_tree(it)` is true. `ordinary_tree` / `tree` are still absent (None) when the worktree cap is off — that is why the old code skipped a None share. With worktrees disabled, a free flight slot, and a ready item that is not tagged `no-worktree`, `flight > 0` is true and `None > 0` raises TypeError, so `ddflow next --lane` crashes instead of offering the item. The new test only covers a configured `worktree.max_parallel`, not a missing tree share.

Running the no-dead-knobs ratchet test after this change will therefore see `swarm.launch_templates_file` as an unreferenced config knob and fail, because it is no longer exempt and is still not consumed.
